authority: open_world_plan_review.typ:605-614 (SimpleLoop 的固定定义) read together with plan:528 (F_r(E*) = scalar(E*), round one)

failure_stage_mapping.note: E* verdict -> trace failure_stage. The trace schema fixes the enum but not this per-runtime mapping; SimpleLoop freezes it here and reports it to the contract owner so the other runtimes can adopt the same one.

note: FROZEN by the a0/contract owner. Adopted verbatim from the SimpleLoop workstream's proposal a0/runtimes/simpleloop/policy/proposed.a0.contract.simpleloop.selection.json, whose scalarization, selection and failure_stage_mapping blocks are themselves copied verbatim from a0/runtimes/simpleloop/policy/simpleloop.policy.json (the source the substrate executed); byte-level equality of all three blocks was re-checked when this was adopted. The scalarization and failure_stage_mapping blocks are A0-wide: every runtime must declare the same null policy and the same E* verdict -> failure_stage table, otherwise plan:577's per-runtime FailureStage counts are not comparable.

scalarization.identity_check: when status == ok the adapter asserts objective.value == fields.sum_radii and fails the candidate otherwise
scalarization.nonfinite: a non-finite scalar (nan/inf) is rejected as an adapter-side measurement error, not compared
scalarization.null_is_not_zero: a null scalar is never coerced to 0.0 or to -inf; an unscored candidate is recorded as unscored and is excluded from the argmax. E* exit 2 / exit 3 propagate as failure_stage values with failure_detail, not as a number.
scalarization.status_gate: scalar is defined iff outcome.status == "ok"; when status is "invalid" or "error" the scalar is null

selection.champion_update: running max over all candidates evaluated so far, so c*_t is monotone and never loses a previously best candidate
selection.epsilon_role: the frozen conformance epsilon (1e-9, EID* Config.conformance.epsilon) is the A0.1 tolerance only; it is NOT applied in selection, so no tolerance window can absorb a score gap (measured below) and no rank transform can either (rank is a monotone map of the value)
selection.order_invariance: c*_t is a function of the set {(candidate_id, scalar)}; permuting the order in which candidates are proposed cannot change the champion
selection.rule: c*_t = argmax over { c_i : i <= t and scalar(c_i) is not null } of scalar(c_i)
selection.tie_break: smallest candidate_id by byte-wise comparison of the UTF-8 encoding of candidate_id
selection.tie_break_alternative_rejected: earliest-evaluation-index (Python max() over a sequence keeps the first maximum) is REJECTED because it is a function of the order in which candidates happened to be considered, and A0.2 requires selection to be invariant to candidate ordering
selection.when_nothing_scored: chosen_candidate_id is null; the run continues with parent = null and the iteration is recorded honestly
